newsitem.title: USA: Interscope president goes back to label.
newsitem.headline: Interscope president goes back to label.

text.p: The president of Interscope Records, the red-hot record label partly owned by Seagram Co. Ltd.'s Universal Music group has apparently decided to stick with the label after walking out late Friday, industry sources said Tuesday.
Over the weekend, a source close to Interscope confirmed Tom Whalley, who is credited with signing acts such as Primus, the Wallflowers and the late Tupac Shakur, had left his post.
Another source familiar with the situation said Walt Disney Co. had approached Whalley a couple of months ago and had made him another offer last week.
On Tuesday, a source close to Disney said "apparently, the deal has not happened and he's back at Interscope."
Another source said that Whalley was on a short list of record industry executives in line to take over struggling Hollywood Records, a unit of Disney.

Whalley has been with Interscope since it opened its doors in 1990. Sources said Whalley signed a lucrative agreement with Interscope. Officials at Disney and Interscope and Universal declined comment.
